text:
Joel Hofer keeps giving St. Louis reasons to lean on him. He has made 17 starts, gone 10-6-1 with a .920 save percentage, and saved 9.8 goals more than an average goalie would on the shots he faced (goals saved above expected), 40 allowed on 49.8 expected, 85th percentile. Last season's +11.0 in 46 games now looks less like a hot year and more like who he is.

Where the edge comes from matters. On low-danger shots he's at .990 against a league .962, worth about seven goals on its own. On high-danger chances he's close to average (.712 against .684, a hair below expected by our measure). That's a goalie who doesn't hand out soft ones, which is how a goalie earns the net. The last two weeks were a mix: a 65-minute shutout at Utah on Nov. 12, four goals against Florida, a strong night in Pittsburgh on Nov. 19, then four more against Edmonton on Sunday. Our talent range still puts his long-run level near league average, so the next stretch of starts will tell you which Hofer is real.
headline: Joel Hofer keeps stopping the easy ones
